page0.text:
I enter the living room.
"Huh? Shirou, did you just come in from the hallway by the front door?"
Illya's sitting alone in the living room.

page1.text:
"Yeah. I stepped outside for a bit. Anything happen while I was out?"
"Not really. But you should be resting in your room, Shirou.
Your body's in just as much danger as Sakura's."

page2.text:
"Yeah, thanks. But it's no big deal so long as the cloth is properly wrapped."
"Oh, you'll collapse if you talk like that!
...Shirou. What happened outside?"

page3.text:
"...Nothing."
"That can't be true! I don't know what you did, but don't talk to me with hollow eyes like that!"

page4.text:
"Ah..."
She got mad at me.
...I must be making a really stupid face right now.
No wonder Illya's upset.

page5.text:
"Sorry. I keep thinking about something, even though I know there's no point in obsessing over it."
I shake my head.
Like Illya says, I can't afford to space out.
I can't face Sakura looking this pathetic either, so I'd better man up!

page6.text:
"Okay, you pass. You look like you're feeling a little better.
So, what did you want to ask me? I'll help you if you want, Shirou."
...

page7.text:
...Oh, man.
Sometimes, Illya can be incredibly kind.
This is the second time she's reached out to help me when I was at my wits' end.
It's hard to tell which of us is older now.

page8.text:
"Okay. Then can I ask you something, Illya?"
"Sure. I'll tell you anything. What do you want to know?"

page9.text:
"...About the Holy Grail. Tell me about the Einzbern's Holy Grail."
"...Ah, you found out. That's one of two things I would have preferred you didn't know."

page10.text:
"Illya. Are you, um..."
"Yeah. I'm a Holy Grail. I was never human to begin with. I'm just a homunculus made to look human."

page11.text:
A homunculus. An artificial human.
In alchemy, there are ways to create life from various magical components, without needing a mother to give birth.
Born from less than respectable methods, homunculi are physically feeble as a general rule.
They're alive like humans and look like humans, but they aren't human. That's how a select few can be created with enormous Magic Circuits.

page12.text:
As living creatures, they're frail.
But as mages—no, as Magic Circuits, homunculi can greatly surpass humans.

page13.text:
"...That's the gist of it.
The Einzberns raised me to be both Holy Grail and Master.
The role of the Holy Grail is to collect the souls of defeated Servants. If it's specialized at that task, it doesn't need to be human. It can even be a literal soup pot. It just needs to have a large enough capacity for containing souls."

page14.text:
Illya speaks flatly.
But this is the first time I've heard that the Holy Grail is meant to collect Servants.

page15.text:
"Of course, it's more like return than recovery.
Servants are summoned by the Holy Grail. Then, they need to return through the Holy Grail once they're defeated, right? I'm the only Einzbern Grail in this town, so I should be the one collecting all of those souls."

page16.text:
"...But there's someone other than me functioning as a Holy Grail.
I realized it when Caster and Lancer were taken. Some other force stronger than me pulled them away.
That's how they've taken most of the Servants.
...I only managed to collect Archer, since he disappeared right in front of me."

page17.text:
...She doesn't need to explain the rest:
the other Holy Grail is Sakura.
According to Illya, Sakura has already taken in Caster and Lancer...even Saber and Berserker, too.

page18.text: "Four Servants' souls... But Illya, can you even keep them under control? I thought the basic rule is that a human body can only contain one soul."

page19.text:
"Yeah. That's doubly true when it comes to Heroic Spirits.
Freed of the molds we call 'classes,' pure Servant souls contain a gigantic amount of magical energy. Taking in even one is like unleashing a typhoon inside your body.
And the Holy Grail is designed to collect seven.
The container can't hold all of them."

page20.text:
"That's why Holy Grails have been soulless, 'nonliving' vessels until now. The Holy Grail's main function is to collect, unify, and control seven Heroic Spirits' worth of souls.
There isn't any room to run unnecessary programs. Any personality the Holy Grail has is erased by its main function."

page21.text:
"What I'm saying, Shirou, is that as the Holy Grail nears completion, it begins to lose its human functions.
That applies to me, too. The more Servants I collect, the more I have to cut out my human functions in order to control them."

page22.text:
"I can repurpose the magical energy that I would use to move my limbs, in order to more finely control the souls.
If I stop breathing, I can stop the souls from leaking out.
If I assign the part of my brain that makes up my personality to pure calculation work, I can stabilize the consolidation of the souls."

page23.text: "The same goes for Sakura. Once she becomes a Holy Grail, her human personality will stop working. She won't be able to afford to stay human."

page24.text:
"Though, I will say...
The difference between me and Sakura is that I can switch over at will, while Sakura is being overwritten. She's an incomplete Black Grail that doesn't have the right to refuse."

page25.text:
Illya explains it all without a hint of emotion.
...Illya knew all along.
She's probably known since she was born. No, even before that.
Her life was created purely for this absurd purpose.

page26.text:
...
Still, there's a silver lining in this.
I breathe a sigh of relief and look up gratefully.

page27.text:
"What is it, Shirou? I said that I'm beyond saving, just like Sakura, you know."
I know that.
I know that, but still.

page28.text:
"You're splitting the souls with Sakura, so you're still okay."
"Hmm. That's true. Sakura's taken most of them, so there isn't anything stopping me from being Illya. Rider and Assassin... Maybe I won't need to lose my human functions even if I take them both."

page29.text:
Right. That's the one saving grace of this situation.
If I were to lose Illya too, it would mean that I failed to protect even a single person.

page30.text:
"E-eh!? Shirou!?"
I realize I'm hugging Illya.
I never made her any promises, nor did she ask for anything.
